# Programming Language Lineage (v5)

<!-- Generated by scripts/generateDatasetRelease.ts from lineage_v5.json. Do not edit by hand. -->

A cited graph of what programming languages and their compilers, runtimes and engines are written in, how they bootstrapped, and which languages influenced which. Browse it at https://www.languagelineage.org/dataset and explore it at https://www.languagelineage.org/explore.

## Contents

| File | Rows | Description |
|---|---:|---|
| `lineage_v5.json` | 191 nodes, 527 edges | Canonical source; every other file is generated from it |
| `lineage_v5_nodes.csv` | 191 | 151 languages and 40 tools (compilers, runtimes, engines) |
| `lineage_v5_edges.csv` | 527 | Directed relationships, each with an evidence URL and a confidence score |

Edges point from the implementation language (or influence) to the thing built with it: `lang:c → lang:python` with `runtime_written_in` means CPython is written in C.

## Relationship types

| Type | Edges |
|---|---:|
| `influenced` | 264 |
| `runtime_written_in` | 115 |
| `compiler_written_in` | 114 |
| `bootstrap_written_in` | 15 |
| `transpiled_to` | 15 |
| `rewritten_in` | 4 |

- `compiler_written_in`, `runtime_written_in`: what an implementation is written in.
- `bootstrap_written_in`: what the first compiler was written in, before self-hosting.
- `rewritten_in`: an implementation moved to a different language.
- `transpiled_to`: a language that compiles to another high-level language.
- `influenced`: design influence, with no code dependency.

"Runs on" (for example Kotlin on the JVM) and compilation targets are not modeled as edges.

## Time

397 of 527 edges (75%) carry a `start_year`; 20 have an `end_year`, meaning the relationship stopped holding (for example Go's compiler was written in C until 2015). An empty `end_year` means the relationship still holds. A `first_release_year` of 0 marks root nodes such as machine code where a year does not apply.

## Sources and confidence

Every edge cites one `evidence_source` URL. 302 of 527 (57%) cite Wikipedia; the rest cite official documentation, source repositories, papers and project announcements. Confidence is a hand-assigned score from 0.65 to 0.99 (median 0.9); it reflects the curator's judgment of the source, not a statistical estimate.

The `source_type` column in the edges CSV is derived from each URL by `scripts/sourceType.ts` (a project's own site, docs or blog counts as project docs):

| source_type | Meaning | Edges |
|---|---|---:|
| `wikipedia` | Wikipedia | 302 |
| `repository` | Source repository | 107 |
| `docs` | Project docs | 105 |
| `paper` | Paper | 6 |
| `article` | Third-party article | 4 |
| `forum` | Forum post | 2 |
| `other` | Other web page | 1 |

## Limitations

- Coverage favors widely used and historically notable languages; it is not a complete catalog (HOPL lists thousands of languages).
- Each edge has one source. Some implementation facts change over time, and a citation can go stale; corrections are welcome as GitHub issues.
- Influence edges record documented, notable influence, not every borrowed feature.
- Logo fields in the JSON point to third-party images under their own licenses and are excluded from the CSV files.
